Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

warn verb

also warning, forewarn, I warned you

classical

Ov. Met. 8.203–206
Cic. Amic. 88

moneō, monēre, monuī, monitum

verb, second conjugation, transitive; with nē or ut + subjunctive

warn, advise

To warn and to advise alike: moneō nē, “I warn you not to”; moneō ut, “I advise you to”.

Other words

  • praemoneō, praemonēre, praemonuī, praemonitum — forewarn

    verb, second conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Verr. 1.23: mē, ut magnopere cavērem, praemonēbat (Lewis & Short)

    To warn beforehand.

  • admoneō, admonēre, admonuī, admonitum — remind; warn

    verb, second conjugation · also used · classical · Lewis & Short s.v. admoneō

    Chiefly “remind” (of what is past, Lewis & Short), but also “warn, urge”.

Examples

  • īnstruit et nātum ‘mediō’que ‘ut līmite currās, Īcare,’ ait ‘moneō, nē, sī dēmissior ībis, unda gravet pennās, sī celsior, ignis adūrat’

    he instructs his son too: ‘I warn you, Icarus, keep to the middle course, so that the sea does not weigh down your wings if you go too low, nor the sun scorch them if you go too high’Ov. Met. 8.203–206

  • nam et monendī amīcī saepe sunt et objūrgandī

    for friends must often be warned and scoldedCic. Amic. 88

See also careful, don’t fall, follow.
